rules.title: Applicable repositories declare Golden Path metadata

applicability.condition: The repository is active, buildable, and organization-managed.

rules.assertion: The repository contains schema-valid .github/golden-path.yaml metadata with explicit profile, artifact, capability, contract, standard, and asset bundle versions.
rules.remediation: Create or update repository-local metadata from the versioned schema and declare only applicable profiles and capabilities.

rules.title: Declared applicability matches repository evidence

applicability.condition: Golden Path metadata is present.

rules.assertion: Declared profiles, artifact types, capabilities, and not-applicable status agree with native manifests, toolchain files, commands, and generated-only or archived evidence.
rules.remediation: Correct stale metadata or migrate the executable repository surface; do not add successful no-op commands to simulate applicability.

rules.title: Applicable repositories expose a root Just façade

applicability.condition: The repository is active and buildable.

rules.assertion: The repository root contains a Just-supported root file exposing init, check, and ci as the stable human and automation entry points.
rules.remediation: Add a root justfile and implement the base commands using native profile commands.

rules.title: Base commands are truthful and non-placeholder

applicability.condition: A base command or declared capability is evaluated.

rules.assertion: Base and capability commands do not succeed through a no-op, placeholder, swallowed failure, or unrelated check.
rules.remediation: Implement the real validation, remove the inapplicable capability declaration, or record an approved time-bounded exception.

rules.title: CI is deterministic and non-mutating

applicability.condition: The ci command is run in a clean checkout with declared prerequisites.

rules.assertion: The ci command composes required repository checks, fails closed, avoids shared-state mutation, and does not depend on undeclared interactive or developer-local state; quality CI and deployment orchestration keep independently reviewable permission, credential, and mutation boundaries.
rules.remediation: Move deployment and repair operations out of ci, establish explicit quality-versus-deployment boundaries, declare prerequisites, and make the command fail when a required check fails.

rules.title: Just composition remains modular and discoverable

applicability.condition: The Justfile contains more than a small direct façade.

rules.assertion: The root Justfile stays thin and delegates cohesive implementation to flat imports, namespaced modules, or repository-local scripts.
rules.remediation: Extract cohesive recipes into imported modules or scripts while retaining stable root commands.

rules.title: Required caller workflows execute the repository CI contract

applicability.condition: A required CI caller workflow validates the repository.

rules.assertion: The caller invokes root just ci or the exact same repository-owned implementation path without reimplementing the quality graph.
rules.remediation: Make the workflow prepare the declared environment and call just ci; remove duplicated or unrelated quality orchestration.

rules.title: Every runtime has one operational version owner

applicability.condition: The repository uses a language runtime or IaC CLI.

rules.assertion: Each toolchain has one declared operational owner: mise for Node.js, Go, Zig and generic CLIs, uv for Python, or rustup for Rust.
rules.remediation: Select the profile owner and remove competing installers or selectors for the same toolchain.

rules.title: Runtime and tool selectors are exact and committed

applicability.condition: A runtime or repository tool is required to build, validate, package, or release.

rules.assertion: Committed toolchain configuration resolves exact supported versions and does not use latest, stable, master, nightly, or an unbounded range.
rules.remediation: Pin the runtime and required tools to an exact supported version in the profile owner file.

rules.title: Mise-managed tools use a committed lock

applicability.condition: mise manages one or more repository tool versions.

rules.assertion: The repository commits mise.toml and mise.lock with a minimum mise compatibility requirement.
rules.remediation: Resolve exact tool versions with the supported mise line, commit the lock, and validate it in CI.

rules.title: Bootstrap and CI use the same declared toolchain

applicability.condition: The repository has local bootstrap and CI execution.

rules.assertion: Local initialization and CI resolve from committed profile authority and do not silently install a different runtime or moving tool version.
rules.remediation: Make both paths invoke the selected owner and fail on unsupported or unresolved versions.

rules.title: Native manifests and resolution records are committed

applicability.condition: The selected profile resolves third-party dependencies.

rules.assertion: The profile-native manifest and required lock or integrity record exist and are committed.
rules.remediation: Generate the profile-native lock or integrity record with the selected manager and commit it with the manifest change.

rules.title: CI dependency preparation is locked or frozen

applicability.condition: CI prepares third-party dependencies.

rules.assertion: CI fails rather than rewriting or resolving beyond the committed native dependency record.
rules.remediation: Use the profile-native frozen, locked, or offline preparation mode and separate explicit update commands.

rules.title: One dependency surface has one native manager

applicability.condition: Multiple manager manifests or locks are detected for one dependency graph.

rules.assertion: Competing package managers do not own or rewrite the same dependency surface.
rules.remediation: Select the profile-native manager, remove obsolete locks, and migrate dependents in a reviewable change.

rules.title: Direct non-registry dependencies are immutable

applicability.condition: A dependency is resolved directly from VCS, URL, archive, binary, or generated source.

rules.assertion: The dependency reference is immutable and integrity-verified where the ecosystem supports verification.
rules.remediation: Replace branch, tag alias, or moving URL references with a full commit SHA, exact digest, or checksummed release.

rules.title: Shared implementation is materialized before runtime

applicability.condition: A repository consumes shared Golden Path configuration, scripts, actions, or workflows.

rules.assertion: Required shared implementation is committed or resolved from an immutable versioned release; normal local and CI commands do not curl and execute mutable remote content.
rules.remediation: Materialize the asset through the approved generator or pin an immutable released artifact with integrity verification.

rules.title: Reusable automation references are immutable

applicability.condition: A repository calls reusable actions, workflows, containers, archives, binaries, or VCS content.

rules.assertion: Executable remote content is pinned by full commit SHA, digest, or exact version plus verified checksum according to its distribution channel.
rules.remediation: Replace mutable branches and tags with immutable identifiers and preserve a readable version annotation where useful.

rules.title: Shared updates are reviewable and version-recorded

applicability.condition: A shared Golden Path asset is added or updated.

rules.assertion: The repository records exact standard and asset bundle versions, materialized changes remain visible in normal review, and the resulting repository passes just ci.
rules.remediation: Run the approved updater in preview mode, commit the reviewable diff, update metadata, and fix just ci before merge.

rules.title: Reusable callers retain least-privilege boundaries

applicability.condition: A caller invokes reusable automation.

rules.assertion: The caller declares minimum permissions, passes only named required secrets, and does not grant reusable code implicit broad authority.
rules.remediation: Reduce caller permissions, replace inherited secret scope with named inputs, and document the trust boundary.

rules.title: Structural conformance is offline and deterministic

applicability.condition: The Golden Path checker evaluates repository structure.

rules.assertion: The structural checker evaluates checked-in data without credentials, network access, repository writes, external API mutation, or time-sensitive advisory claims.
rules.remediation: Move external evidence to an explicit online adapter and keep the core structural evaluation read-only and reproducible.

rules.title: Checker output, CI summary, and exit codes follow the versioned contract

applicability.condition: A checker or CI adapter emits a conformance result.

rules.assertion: Machine output validates against golden-path-checker-output/v1, CI emits the bounded actionable summary required by the standard, and the process exit code reflects fail, error, warning-policy, and incomplete-evaluation semantics.
rules.remediation: Emit schema-valid findings with stable rule IDs, include the required versions, profiles, counts, applicable expiry, and remediation in the CI summary, and return the contract-defined exit status.

rules.title: Enforcement state is reported truthfully

applicability.condition: Conformance output describes hosting-platform enforcement.

rules.assertion: A CI failure is not labeled platform-enforced unless the actual repository plan and settings prevent bypass or merge.
rules.remediation: Report report-only or ci-failing and provide separately verified platform enforcement evidence.

rules.title: Absent conformance execution is not a pass

applicability.condition: A policy, workflow, or platform gate interprets the conformance result.

rules.assertion: A missing, skipped, cancelled, stale, or wrong-revision checker result is not interpreted as a passing result.
rules.remediation: Require positive evidence from the stable check identity for the exact source revision and preserve incomplete evaluation as non-passing.

rules.title: MUST deviations use scoped expiring exceptions

applicability.condition: An applicable MUST or MUST_NOT rule is knowingly unmet.

rules.assertion: A schema-valid exception names the rule, bounded scope and reason, accountable owner, risk class, durable approving authority, approval date, and expiry.
rules.remediation: Fix the violation or add the minimum approved time-bounded exception; SHOULD deviations and accepted non-remediation variations do not create ceremonial issues.

rules.title: High-risk exceptions carry independent approval and controls

applicability.condition: The exception concerns security, release integrity, supply chain, destructive state, broad privilege, or another classified high-risk rule.

rules.assertion: The exception records risk, compensating controls, remediation tracking, and at least two distinct approving authorities including independent review.
rules.remediation: Obtain independent approval and document bounded compensating controls before relying on the exception.

rules.title: Policy, shared implementation, and repository execution remain separate

applicability.condition: A policy document, shared implementation, or repository adoption change is reviewed.

rules.assertion: Normative meaning stays in the central standard, shared code implements that meaning, and repository-local files remain the executable As-built authority.
rules.remediation: Move normative rules to the standard and keep implementation locators, repository status, and migration work outside the policy contract.

rules.title: Public shared implementation preserves a safe release boundary

applicability.condition: A generic shared implementation is distributed from a public repository.

rules.assertion: Public source, fixtures, logs, workflow data, and release assets contain no restricted data; maintainers own release permission and vulnerability reporting.
rules.remediation: Remove restricted material, establish a security policy and maintainer-only release boundary, or use an approved restricted distribution.

rules.title: Workflow templates materialize thin least-privilege callers

applicability.condition: An organization workflow template is published.

rules.assertion: The template has matching metadata, valid workflow syntax, minimum permissions, and a repository-owned caller that delegates quality behavior to just ci.
rules.remediation: Correct template metadata and syntax, reduce permissions, and remove repository-specific quality logic from the starter.

rules.title: Shared implementation has an immutable cross-language baseline

applicability.condition: A shared checker, generator, CLI, or asset bundle is released for cross-repository consumption.

rules.assertion: An immutable GitHub Release asset provides supported platform archives, per-asset checksums, manifest, changelog, provenance, and clean-build/test evidence without requiring GitHub Packages.
rules.remediation: Publish the complete immutable baseline release and keep ecosystem registries as optional additional channels.

rules.title: Selected runtime lines have an organization disposition

applicability.condition: A language runtime or compiler is selected.

rules.assertion: The exact selected runtime resolves to preferred, supported, or explicitly time-bounded compatibility-only in the current runtime-support catalog.
rules.remediation: Upgrade to a preferred or supported exact version, or record a bounded compatibility exception and migration.

rules.title: EOL and blocked runtime lines fail conformance

applicability.condition: The selected exact runtime is EOL, prerelease-only, or organization-blocked.

rules.assertion: An EOL, prerelease, or blocked line is not treated as supported merely because existing repositories still use it.
rules.remediation: Create owned migration work and move to a supported line; use an exception only for a bounded operational need.

rules.title: Node and pnpm authority is exact and native

applicability.condition: The Node.js and TypeScript profile applies.

rules.assertion: Node.js is exact and supported through mise, packageManager pins exact pnpm, and pnpm-lock.yaml is committed and frozen in CI.
rules.remediation: Pin supported Node.js and pnpm versions, regenerate the native lock, and use frozen install in CI.

rules.title: TypeScript quality tools have separated responsibilities

applicability.condition: The corresponding capability is declared.

rules.assertion: Prettier owns formatting, ESLint owns lint, and tsc --noEmit performs an explicit separate typecheck using supported configuration.
rules.remediation: Add the missing native command, remove overlapping formatter authority, and keep type analysis independently visible.

rules.title: TypeScript module and build semantics are explicit

applicability.condition: The repository builds or publishes JavaScript or TypeScript output.

rules.assertion: Module format, package exports, source maps, declaration output, and build ownership are explicit for the selected artifact.
rules.remediation: Declare ESM or intentional dual output and make package metadata agree with emitted files.

rules.title: External Node libraries validate packed output

applicability.condition: The library is published outside the repository or consumed as a packaged artifact.

rules.assertion: CI inspects or installs the packed artifact and validates exports, files, types, runtime compatibility, and publish contents.
rules.remediation: Add a deterministic pack validation step and correct package exports or files before publishing.

rules.title: Node package publication uses an immutable approved release path

applicability.condition: A Node package is published to an external registry.

rules.assertion: Publication runs only from an immutable release ref in an approved workflow, uses trusted publishing where supported, and emits provenance for a supported public npm package.
rules.remediation: Disable local and pull-request publication, use the approved release workflow, and add trusted publishing and provenance or a bounded credential exception.

rules.title: Python uses uv as runtime and dependency authority

applicability.condition: The Python profile applies.

rules.assertion: pyproject.toml is authoritative, uv owns Python and dependency resolution, .python-version is exact, and uv.lock is committed and frozen in CI.
rules.remediation: Migrate runtime and dependency preparation to uv, pin a supported Python version, and commit the lock.

rules.title: Python quality uses Ruff, mypy, and pytest

applicability.condition: The corresponding Python capability is declared.

rules.assertion: Ruff owns formatting and lint, mypy owns static type analysis, and pytest runs real repository tests for declared capabilities.
rules.remediation: Configure and expose each applicable quality command or remove an inapplicable capability declaration.

rules.title: Python packaging and workspace boundaries are explicit

applicability.condition: The Python artifact is packaged, published, or uses a workspace.

rules.assertion: The build backend, package contents, workspace members, native boundary, supported Python range, and artifact validation are explicit.
rules.remediation: Declare the backend and artifact metadata, validate built wheel and sdist contents, and align native build tooling with the package contract.

rules.title: Python native dependency variants resolve deterministically

applicability.condition: The dependency graph has CPU, CUDA, ROCm, or another host-sensitive native variant.

rules.assertion: CI and production locks do not change dependency selection through host-driver auto-detection; a named index, marker, or profile input selects the variant.
rules.remediation: Declare the native variant explicitly and regenerate the lock without host-dependent selection.

rules.title: Go runtime, module, and workspace authority align

applicability.condition: The Go profile applies.

rules.assertion: mise pins an exact supported Go release and go.mod or go.work directives do not contradict the selected toolchain.
rules.remediation: Pin a supported exact Go release and align native module or workspace directives.

rules.title: Go dependencies and tools use native records

applicability.condition: The Go profile resolves modules or repository tools.

rules.assertion: go.mod and applicable go.sum are committed, tidy state is checked, Go 1.24+ project tools use the tool directive and go tool, and external support CLIs use exact verified assets.
rules.remediation: Commit tidy module records, move project tools to the native tool directive, and pin external support CLIs through the release contract.

rules.title: Go format, vet, lint, and tests are real gates

applicability.condition: The corresponding Go capability is declared.

rules.assertion: gofmt, go vet, golangci-lint v2, and go test execute against the applicable packages without hiding failures.
rules.remediation: Expose the native checks through Just, pin golangci-lint v2, and correct exclusions or placeholders.

rules.title: Concurrent Go artifacts provide a supported race lane

applicability.condition: The artifact is an application, service, or concurrent library and a supported Linux race lane is technically applicable.

rules.assertion: The repository runs a supported Linux race lane for the applicable packages and reports a real failure.
rules.remediation: Add the race lane, record why the artifact is not applicable, or use a time-bounded exception for a technical blocker.

rules.title: Go fuzz, coverage, and package validation follow artifact risk

applicability.condition: The artifact exposes parser, security, public module, binary, or release risk that benefits from a bounded optional lane.

rules.assertion: Fuzzing, coverage, and packaged binary or module validation are selected according to real parser, boundary, and release risk.
rules.remediation: Add the applicable risk-based lane and document why an expensive or irrelevant lane is omitted.

rules.title: Rust uses an exact rustup toolchain

applicability.condition: The Rust profile applies.

rules.assertion: rust-toolchain.toml pins an exact supported release and rustup is the sole Rust toolchain owner.
rules.remediation: Replace moving stable or nightly selectors with the supported exact release and remove competing mise Rust ownership.

rules.title: Cargo package and lock policy matches the artifact

applicability.condition: The Rust profile applies.

rules.assertion: Cargo.toml declares edition, resolver, rust-version, and workspace boundaries, and every Golden Path Rust repository commits one root Cargo.lock.
rules.remediation: Align Cargo metadata with the exact compiler, generate the root Cargo.lock, and commit it for applications, services, CLIs, and libraries alike.

rules.title: Rust formatting, Clippy, and tests fail on findings

applicability.condition: The corresponding Rust capability is declared.

rules.assertion: cargo fmt --check, Clippy with warnings denied, and real Cargo tests cover the declared workspace and feature policy.
rules.remediation: Expose and enforce the native Cargo checks through the root command contract.

rules.title: Rust unsafe policy is explicit and reviewed

applicability.condition: The Rust profile applies, whether or not unsafe is present.

rules.assertion: The repository declares safe-only or unsafe-permitted and validates or documents every unsafe boundary, invariant, and reviewer expectation.
rules.remediation: Deny unsafe code for safe-only artifacts or document and test narrowly scoped unsafe-permitted boundaries.

rules.title: Zig is conditional and pins an exact tagged stable

applicability.condition: Zig source, generated bindings, or a Zig toolchain participates in a required build.

rules.assertion: The profile is declared and mise pins an exact organization-approved tagged Zig release rather than master or nightly.
rules.remediation: Declare the appropriate Zig profile and pin the current approved stable baseline.

rules.title: Zig packages and generated bindings are reproducible

applicability.condition: The build uses Zig dependencies, build.zig.zon, or generated Zig, C, or foreign-language bindings.

rules.assertion: Package dependencies are immutable and hashed, and generated surfaces have committed source authority plus deterministic regeneration and clean-diff validation.
rules.remediation: Pin and hash Zig dependencies, define the generator command, and validate that regeneration produces no unexplained diff.

rules.title: Zig tests, safety, optimization, and targets reflect use

applicability.condition: Zig participates in a required build or shipped artifact.

rules.assertion: The required build has real tests and declares safety, optimization, target, C ABI, and linkage assumptions that affect the artifact.
rules.remediation: Add representative build and test lanes and make cross-target or C integration assumptions explicit.

rules.title: Each infrastructure resource has one write owner

applicability.condition: The repository declares a stateful infrastructure profile.

rules.assertion: Every managed resource has one engine, one state boundary, and one routine write owner, and engine migration has a separate approved plan.
rules.remediation: Remove overlapping ownership or establish a migration ADR covering identity, import, replacement, state, secrets, rollback, and verification.

rules.title: Static IaC CI does not mutate shared state

applicability.condition: The repository executes its static check or ci lane.

rules.assertion: Static validation, typecheck, test, synth, format, init, and validate do not mutate shared cloud resources or state.
rules.remediation: Move dynamic lookups and state mutation into the owned stateful delivery lane and preserve a credential-free static path where feasible.

rules.title: Stateful IaC delivery satisfies bounded safety outcomes

applicability.condition: Automation mutates shared infrastructure or state.

rules.assertion: Delivery uses short-lived least privilege, validates the exact target, prevents collisions, previews current code before apply, protects sensitive state, separates destructive repair, and records bounded success evidence.
rules.remediation: Add the missing delivery outcome in the owning deployment contract and repository workflow before allowing state mutation.

rules.title: Risky IaC changes require independent approval

applicability.condition: The operation deletes or replaces persistent resources, weakens protection, destroys production, changes state ownership or backend, has large blast radius, or force-unlocks a collision.

rules.assertion: A distinct authorized person or equivalent independent control approves the classified high-risk operation using durable evidence.
rules.remediation: Route the operation through the bounded approval and operator path; do not require two-person approval for routine low-risk deployments.

rules.title: AWS CDK preserves local dependency and CloudFormation safety

applicability.condition: The AWS CDK profile applies.

rules.assertion: CDK libraries and CLI are exact local dependencies, static ci synthesizes without deployment, routine deployment does not bootstrap, and production uses CloudFormation change sets and rollback without hotswap.
rules.remediation: Pin local CDK dependencies, separate bootstrap, and restore deterministic synth plus normal CloudFormation production safety.

rules.title: Terraform and OpenTofu preserve one exact lock owner

applicability.condition: A Terraform or OpenTofu root is selected.

rules.assertion: Each root selects one exact engine, commits provider constraints and .terraform.lock.hcl, pins modules immutably, validates without state mutation, and protects stored plans as sensitive.
rules.remediation: Select one engine owner, regenerate its provider lock deliberately, pin modules, and move stateful plan/apply behavior to the delivery lane.

rules.title: Pulumi preserves exact pins and a fresh production preview

applicability.condition: The Pulumi profile applies.

rules.assertion: Pulumi project, CLI, SDK, provider, host dependencies, and locks are exact; plaintext secrets are absent; production up previews the current target and never skips preview.
rules.remediation: Commit exact Pulumi and host-language authority, remove plaintext secrets, and require a fresh target preview in the stateful delivery lane.

rules.title: Known-vulnerability signals have an accountable path

applicability.condition: The repository resolves third-party dependencies.

rules.assertion: The repository receives a current known-vulnerability signal and has an owner-visible remediation or approved exception path.
rules.remediation: Enable an ecosystem-supported alert or audit and assign unresolved findings to an accountable remediation path.

rules.title: Dependency automation follows normal validation policy

applicability.condition: Dependabot, Renovate, or another automated updater opens or merges changes.

rules.assertion: Automated changes run the same configured checks and review or merge policy as equivalent human changes, and two bots do not own the same dependency surface.
rules.remediation: Align bot changes with the repository CI and ownership boundary, or remove overlapping automation.

rules.title: CI caches cannot become trusted dependency or release authority

applicability.condition: A CI cache is enabled.

rules.assertion: Cache keys cover result-affecting inputs, cache content is not dependency or release authority, and a cache miss remains rebuildable from native manifests and locks.
rules.remediation: Strengthen keys, separate native stores from generated executable output, and prove a clean rebuild without cache state.

rules.title: CI caches preserve secret and trust boundaries

applicability.condition: A CI cache is writable from workflows with different trust levels or may contain sensitive or executable material.

rules.assertion: Caches exclude sensitive material and low-trust forks, pull_request_target, or issue-driven workflows cannot write a trusted shared cache.
rules.remediation: Remove secrets and signing or state material, separate trust domains, and restrict shared-cache writes to hardened trusted triggers.

rules.title: External compiled releases carry a digest-bound SBOM

applicability.condition: A compiled artifact is externally published, customer-delivered, or contractually regulated.

rules.assertion: An SPDX or CycloneDX SBOM represents resolved final-build components and binds to the released artifact digest without secrets or unnecessary internal paths.
rules.remediation: Generate the SBOM from the final artifact, bind and store it with release evidence, and remove sensitive data.

rules.title: Production and external releases should carry verified provenance

applicability.condition: The artifact is externally or canonically released.

rules.assertion: Release evidence connects artifact digest, source commit, builder identity, and workflow, and consumers verify those expectations when provenance is a gate.
rules.remediation: Add Free-compatible signed release metadata or an attestation plus explicit consumer verification.

rules.title: Consumers verify usable provenance before required execution

applicability.condition: A required build, bootstrap, deployment, or release artifact provides usable provenance evidence.

rules.assertion: Consumption verifies the artifact subject digest, signature, builder identity, and expected source and workflow before execution or promotion.
rules.remediation: Add plan-compatible attestation or signed-manifest verification and fail closed when identity or digest expectations do not match.

rules.title: Supported platform claims have representative validation

applicability.condition: The repository claims production, release, public OS, architecture, runtime, or feature support.

rules.assertion: At least one production or release representative lane is canonical, and every publicly promised platform combination is validated.
rules.remediation: Add representative validation or narrow the documented support claim; do not require an irrelevant full Cartesian matrix.

rules.title: Development containers preserve repository authority

applicability.condition: A Dev Container or equivalent repository development image is adopted.

rules.assertion: Container configuration is repository-local, immutable, non-secret, separate from production images, and subordinate to native manifests, toolchain owners, and root commands.
rules.remediation: Pin images and features, inject rather than commit secrets, separate development from production images, and retain native authority.

rules.title: Privileged development containers receive explicit risk review

applicability.condition: A development container uses privileged mode, broad capabilities, a host Docker socket, credential mounts, or public forwarding.

rules.assertion: The elevated host or credential boundary has explicit risk review, minimum scope, and a time-bounded exception when it cannot meet the safe baseline.
rules.remediation: Remove the elevated access or record the narrow security exception with independent approval and compensating controls.

rules.title: Golden Path standard versions use CalVer

applicability.condition: A standard, schema, catalog, asset bundle, or checker release is identified.

rules.assertion: Normative standard versions use YYYY.MM with a positive patch only when needed, while schemas and executable artifacts retain their separate compatibility versions.
rules.remediation: Use the correct version axis and do not encode product or repository release versions into the Golden Path standard.

rules.title: Released standard and asset snapshots are immutable

applicability.condition: A Golden Path release is published or consumed.

rules.assertion: A published version is never rewritten and its release manifest binds normative source, catalog, schemas, assets, and integrity digests.
rules.remediation: Publish a new version and retain the prior immutable snapshot with explicit compatibility metadata.

rules.title: Compatibility and retirement remain explicit

applicability.condition: A rule, schema, checker, asset bundle, or runtime line changes lifecycle state.

rules.assertion: The release records compatibility, deprecation, replacement, rollout state, and retirement without reusing stable IDs or silently converting warning to failure.
rules.remediation: Add explicit lifecycle metadata and publish the change in a new immutable standard or artifact version.

rules.title: Required enforcement waits for a stable implementation release

applicability.condition: A shared implementation result is promoted from report-only to a required organization control.

rules.assertion: The implementation is at least 1.0.0 and has passed compatibility, rollback, supported-platform, and migration fixtures before required enforcement.
rules.remediation: Keep the 0.x release report-only until stable compatibility and operational evidence are complete.
